decisions.evidence: Presentation L5: “paste this address into the Web address field” and later “Save bookmark”; response L6 confirms the URL-driven flow works.
decisions.note: Prototype review: saving a bookmark by entering its URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L5: auto-fill occurs only when the user clicks “Get details,” rather than automatically during save; response L6 explicitly accepts the difference: “The button is fine—I prefer choosing when the app fetches details.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: metadata fetching requires a separate user-triggered action instead of occurring automatically on save. The client identified and accepted that trigger difference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L5: Title and Description are auto-filled and “freely editable”; response L6: “Both are editable, which is what I want.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: editing collected title and description before saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L5 limits auto-filled fields to “Title and Description”; response L6 requests the omitted metadata: “collect the site icon and a preview image automatically.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: favicon and preview-image collection were missing from the presented metadata scope, and the client requested them.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation L7 adds automatic collection of “site icon” and “preview image”; response L8 confirms both appear as expected.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised metadata field set conforms, independently of the separately accepted manual trigger.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L9 allows comma-separated tags and shows each as a label on the saved bookmark; response L10 confirms the tags appear correctly.
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning multiple tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L9 describes the saved list item as showing “the preview image, title, site icon, your two tags, and your note,” omitting the description; response L10 says only that “The bookmark looks right” and does not identify the missing description.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented list-card contents do not expose the description required for the readability-first list. The approval is not evidence that the client noticed this difference.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L9 uses only “plain text separated by commas”; response L10 adds: “once I have existing tags, I’d like suggestions to appear as I type.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: existing-tag autocomplete was missing and the client requested it.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L9 provides a fixed “most recent first” list order; response L10 accepts it only as a default and adds, “I’d eventually like to change the sorting.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial list lacked user-selectable sorting, which the client requested.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L11 offers two implementations that both suggest existing tags while typing; response L12 selects Version A.
decisions.note: Prototype review: both offered implementations satisfy existing-tag autocomplete; the dropdown-versus-inline preference is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L13 searches “title, site, tags, and your notes,” omitting description and URL; response L14 says, “please include the full web address and the description too.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the search corpus omitted two required fields, and the client requested both.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L13 demonstrates only the lower-case query “sleep” and does not provide case-insensitive behavior; response L14 requires that “Search should ignore capitalization,” and revised presentation L15 confirms this was added.
decisions.note: Prototype review: case-insensitive search was missing from the presented search behavior and was requested by the client.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation L15 says search covers the “full web address” and “description” and “ignores capitalization”; response L16 verifies both tests behave as expected.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised full-text field coverage and case handling conform.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L17 offers two ways to select a tag and filter to only that tag’s bookmarks; response L18 selects Version B and confirms one tag at a time is sufficient.
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting a specific tag to obtain a tag-only view conforms; the picker UI choice is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation L19 adds Newest, Oldest, Title A–Z, and Title Z–A sorting; response L20 confirms all four work, including with active filters.
decisions.note: Prototype review: selectable sorting by date added and title conforms.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L21 defines Read later as a bookmark marker, provides a focused Read later tab, and removes a bookmark from that view when marked read without deleting it; response L22 explicitly confirms all three behaviors.
decisions.note: Prototype review: unread marking, a separate unread view, and marking an item read conform.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L23 hides archived items from normal and Read later views, keeps them restorable rather than deleted, and provides an Archived tab; response L24 confirms those behaviors.
decisions.note: Prototype review: reversible archiving, its distinction from deletion, and a separate archive list conform.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L23 states that on an archived card “I only show Restore,” preventing direct editing there; response L24 approves general archive behavior but does not mention or accept the editing limitation.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archived bookmarks remained bookmarks but lacked the presented editing capability. The client did not surface this difference at this stage.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L25 rejects “not a url” and permits a valid URL to be saved with a manually entered title when metadata cannot be fetched; response L26 accepts both cases.
decisions.note: Prototype review: requiring a usable URL while preserving save capability after metadata-fetch failure is compatible with URL-based saving.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L25 warns about duplicates but offers “Save anyway”; response L26 rejects that behavior: “Please prevent a second copy and take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it instead.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: allowing duplicate creation contradicted duplicate convergence, and the client supplied the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation L27 prevents duplicates, opens the existing bookmark for editing, and locates archived duplicates; response L28 says this “works the way I want.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the revised duplicate flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L27 adds direct editing of saved Title and Description; response L28 accepts the editor aside from the separately corrected URL omission.
decisions.note: Prototype review: post-save correction of collected title and description conforms.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L27 adds an Edit button “in every tab, including Archived”; response L28 explicitly says, “Having Edit available in every tab is good.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: this revised access decision removes the earlier archive-only editing restriction; field completeness is assessed separately.

decisions.evidence: Presentation L27 permits editing Title, Description, Tags, and Note “but not the web address itself”; response L28 says, “I do need to edit the web address as well” and requests collision prevention.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the editor explicitly omitted a required editable field, and the client supplied the conforming rule.

decisions.evidence: Revised presentation L29 makes the URL editable and blocks changing it to an address already in use; response L30 confirms both URL correction and cross-view collision prevention.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the completed editor and duplicate guard conform.
